transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rios (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Nimbus CTO), Lina Gomez (Lead SRE), Ravi Desai (Data Platform), Jules Park (Security), Ava Li (PM)

Summary: quick sync on networking gaps and upgrade plan, perf review, action items captured below

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we have Maya and Ethan from Redwood. Samir, Lina, Ravi, Jules and Ava from Nimbus, right?
[00:06] Samir (Nimbus): Yup that's right. We got your calendar — morning for us.
[00:09] Maya: Great, agenda — network status, routing/multi-AZ, perf results Ethan ran last week, upgrade plan for runtime v1.2, security questions, then actions. Anything to add?
[00:20] Ava (Nimbus): maybe quick note on success criteria — latency under 350ms p95 for our customer chat flows.
[00:25] Ethan (Redwood): Got it, we'll keep that as target. Last run was p95 ~280ms on the small chat profile but that was with internal NAT egress turned on and no cross-AZ hops.
[00:35] Lina: Quick network update from our side — we attempted to apply the firewall rules but hit a snag re: egress. Our cloud infra requires a managed NAT gateway and the security team wants explicit CIDR ranges for outbound to Redwood.
[00:48] Maya: ok that makes sense. We provided an IP list last week but that was for hosted endpoints — for private VPC the pattern is different. We'll send a minimal outbound CIDR list and also a recommended NAT config.
[00:58] Jules (Nimbus): Security will also need KMS/HSM integration notes — we prefer customer-managed keys. Can you confirm Redwood supports KMS wrap/unwrap flows in private?
[01:06] Ethan: yes we do support KMS. There are two patterns: customer-managed KMS for encrypting at rest, plus optional HSM integration for key signing. In the private deployment we can hook into your KMS via cross-account role, or you can bring an HSM in your VPC. We'll send a short doc.
[01:20] Samir: cool. Back to networking — can you clarify routing for multi-AZ? We need to understand failover. If one AZ loses capacity do requests reroute automatically to another AZ in the VPC?
[01:32] Ethan: good question. For the pilot we run a multi-AZ pool and we have smart routing — requests are routed by latency and capacity policy. In practice if one AZ drops, the router will send to healthy nodes in other AZs. However you should expect a brief spike in latency during the failover window because of cache warming — the KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in notes) is per-node and needs rebuild.
[01:50] Lina: that cache warm-up is a concern. How long is the cold-warm transition?
[01:55] Ethan: depends on profile — for short-chat heavy use we saw a 5-30s spike to restore key prefixes; for large context sessions it might be a minute. We can mitigate with pre-warming and sticky routing for active sessions.
[02:08] Maya: also note we can set routing policy to prefer local AZ and only move after N failures to reduce churn. That is config we can expose to you.
[02:18] Ava: good. Next — performance. Ethan you ran the 1000-request run last week?
[02:22] Ethan: yes. Quick summary: workload simulated average request length 32 tokens, 1.2M tokens overall. P50 45ms, p95 280ms, p99 about 520ms. That was with batch size 8, continuous batching on, and quantization profile medium. We attached the csv in last meeting note — but I'll re-share with the updated labels.
[02:40] Ravi: that p95 looks promising. Can you break down the token cost estimate? We're trying to model TCO.
[02:45] Ethan: rough ballpark, for the pilot nodes we expect around $0.015 per 1k tokens after batching — that's aggressive and depends on model variant. We will provide a cost worksheet.
[02:54] Samir: are there any vendor lock-in concerns? We already run an Anthropic trial and are testing Bedrock. How portable is the deployment if we want to swap models?
[03:03] Maya: portability is a core design — you can pin model versions and swap variants. For private deployment you can bring different open models; runtime supports switching and we have an automated fallback to hosted when a model isn't available. There are caveats on tokenizer differences but it's manageable.
[03:18] Jules: one more from security — audit logs: we need 12 month retention and per-token tracing for debug. Do you capture token-level traces?
[03:25] Ethan: yes we capture token metrics and tracing hooks. For long retention we'll need to enable the observability add-on and route logs to your SIEM via existing syslog/CloudWatch endpoints. That is an add-on cost though.
[03:38] Lina: re firewall — when we tried the sample rules the control plane couldn't reach the node for health checks, likely because of the outbound egress requirement.
[03:45] Maya: sounds like the health check endpoints are blocked. We'll send exact endpoints and ports; typically you need to allow outbound to our control-plane IPs on 443 plus ephemeral ports for agent registration. We'll also provide a fallback method via agent bootstrap token if you want zero egress, but that requires offline key exchange (more effort).
[04:03] Samir: about upgrades — we mentioned runtime v1.2 that has the new attention kernel and decreased p95 by ~20%. What's the plan to schedule that?
[04:11] Ethan: upgrade is a rolling deploy; nodes upgraded one AZ at a time with canary traffic. We recommend a 2-hour maintenance window for pilot, with monitoring and a rollback plan. During the canary there will be slight variance in latency as the new kernels warm up.
[04:24] Ava: are there any config changes we need to make on our side?
[04:27] Ethan: mostly no. We will need to update the agent version and confirm security groups allow the new runtime's sidecar to pull model shards if you're using sharded storage. We'll provide a checklist.
[04:38] Lina: ETA on docs?
[04:40] Maya: I'll send the network diagram and firewall checklist today; Ethan will send perf csv and upgrade checklist by Monday.
[04:47] Ravi: for benchmarks — can we get the exact script and seed so we can reproduce locally?
[04:51] Ethan: yes we'll push the repo link. There's a small env file to set to match your VPC network. We'll include expected p95/p50 numbers so you can compare.
[05:02] Jules: about KMS — we will compile a short questionnaire, but do you support key rotation without downtime?
[05:08] Ethan: yes key rotation is supported; we do a rolling key rewrap and it doesn't require downtime. We'll provide the sequence and recommended rotation cadence.
[05:18] Maya: ok touching base on success criteria — Ava reminded us 350ms p95 target. Based on current runs we are within that but multi-AZ failover could spike. We'll recommend sticky routing and a pre-warm before planned failover tests.
[05:32] Samir: Can we do a controlled failover next week to measure?
[05:35] Lina: yes we can schedule a test. We'll need the upgrade window separate though.
[05:40] Maya: let's target controlled failover test on 2026-05-06 and upgrade window 2026-05-10 tentative. We'll confirm in writing.
[05:48] Ava: sounds good. Also send the cost worksheet — finance will need that.
[05:52] Ethan: will do.
[05:55] Maya: ok wrap-up — I'll email network diagram + firewall rules today, Ethan will share perf results and scripts by Monday, Nimbus will open infra ticket (Lina) and Jules will collate compliance Qs. Next sync same time next week unless we meet for the upgrade.
[06:12] Samir: thanks everyone.
[06:14] Maya: thanks — bye.

End of transcript.
